liquidationPreference.label: Liquidation preference
liquidationPreference.hint: The most important preferred-share right: investors get paid before founders and the team. Standard is 1x, but it can increase with negotiation.

protectiveProvisions.label: Protective provisions
protectiveProvisions.hint: As a minority, the fund needs vetoes on key decisions — debt, issuances, business changes. Aim for balance with operating autonomy.

liquidityRights.label: Liquidity rights
liquidityRights.hint: Defines how and when investors can demand an exit if there is no liquidity event within 7–10 years.

dragAlong.label: Drag-along threshold
dragAlong.hint: The single most sensitive number in the document. Our default is 75%. It decides when you can be forced to sell.

antiDilution.label: Anti-dilution type
antiDilution.hint: A broad-based weighted average is gentle. A full ratchet is harsh. Know which one protects the investor here.

vesting.label: Founder vesting
vesting.hint: You earn your shares over four years. Leave before the one-year cliff and you usually keep nothing.

preamble.title: Agreement introduction
preamble.summary: Identifies the company, lead investor, and effective date for shareholder rules.
preamble.why: Without clear parties and timing, a fund cannot tell who each clause binds or when it applies in your round.

1.title: Purpose of the agreement
1.summary: States that this pact governs shareholder rights and obligations in a Colombian venture investment.
1.why: Signals to investors that governance, transfers, dilution, and exit are covered here — not just generic bylaws.

2.title: Transfer restrictions
2.summary: Limits share sales without meeting right of first refusal and other corporate rules.
2.why: Protects the cap table from unwanted third-party buyers without giving other holders a chance to respond.

3.title: Drag-along
3.summary: If a minimum percentage approves a sale, other shareholders must sell on the same terms.
3.why: This is the buyer's lever to acquire 100% of the company. A low threshold exposes you to being dragged into a sale you do not want.

4.title: Tag-along
4.summary: Lets minority holders join a majority sale on a proportional basis.
4.why: Protects founders and other minorities from being left behind while a majority shareholder exits.

5.title: Anti-dilution
5.summary: Adjusts conversion price or investor protection if future issuances happen at a lower price.
5.why: Defines how much extra dilution you take if the next round is priced lower. Broad-based is usually more negotiable than full ratchet.

6.title: Shareholder decisions
6.summary: Lists decisions requiring a qualified majority — new series, material debt, key asset sales, etc.
6.why: Marks what the CEO or board cannot decide alone without shareholders holding enough voting power.

7.title: Founder vesting and departure
7.summary: Incorporates the vesting agreement by reference and good/bad leaver rules.
7.why: Connects corporate governance with founder retention. Investors will check whether your equity is truly earned over time.

8.title: Confidentiality
8.summary: Keeps economic and strategic terms of the pact confidential.
8.why: Prevents leaks about valuation, preferences, and rights that could affect negotiations with other funds.

9.title: Dispute resolution
9.summary: Sets arbitration or ordinary courts for shareholder disputes.
9.why: Anticipates where and how conflicts are resolved. In Colombian venture, arbitration is often faster than ordinary litigation.

10.title: Governing law
10.summary: Fixes Colombian law and contractual domicile city.
10.why: Anchors the agreement to local law and a known forum — relevant for international funds investing in Colombia.

preamble.title: Term sheet framework
preamble.summary: Summarizes the preferred-share investment offer, what is binding (confidentiality), and what remains subject to definitive agreements.
preamble.why: Only confidentiality and exclusivity are typically binding at signing. Everything else is a negotiation baseline until subscription and shareholders agreements close.

1.title: Offer terms
1.summary: Sets closing, investors, amount, price per share, post-money valuation, cap table, and use of proceeds.
1.why: Investors expect preferred shares, not common. The amount defines ownership %; post-money valuation locks that percentage before the round closes.

2.title: Dividends
2.summary: Governs if and when dividends are paid on preferred shares and blocks distributions for several years.
2.why: Should align with the business plan. It can reassure funds that capital will not be used to pay founders until meaningful traction is achieved.

3.title: Liquidation preference
3.summary: Defines how much preferred holders receive before common holders in a liquidation, sale, or similar event.
3.why: This is the core economic right of preferred shares. Standard is 1x the investment; in bridge rounds we have seen up to 3x depending on risk and leverage.

4.title: Voting rights
4.summary: Preferred shares vote on an as-converted basis, elect an investor director, and common shares may carry multiple votes.
4.why: Favors founders if common shares carry more weight or multiple votes. One vote per share is standard; control should remain majority founder-held in early stages.

5.title: Protective provisions
5.summary: Lists decisions requiring preferred-holder consent — issuances, debt, business changes, etc.
5.why: As a minority, the fund needs vetoes. Includes the debt threshold without consent: a key autonomy vs. oversight decision.

6.title: Optional conversion
6.summary: Allows preferred shares to convert 1:1 into common at the holder's option.
6.why: Gives investors flexibility to move into common shares when useful, for example before an exit or a later round.

7.title: Subscription agreement
7.summary: Covers representations, warranties, closing conditions, and allocation of legal fees.
7.why: Conditions precedent protect the investor between term sheet signing and closing. Founders prefer specific conditions; funds prefer broad wording.

8.title: Information rights
8.summary: Access to facilities, periodic reports, annual budget, and updated cap table.
8.why: Standard rights that let investors monitor the company. Ideally share information founders already use without excessive team overhead.

9.title: Pro rata rights
9.summary: Lets investors and founders participate in future rounds to avoid dilution.
9.why: An important concession for funds and usually easy to grant: it preserves their option to keep investing in the company.

10.title: Supermajority and non-compete
10.summary: Sensitive board decisions (CEO, budget, auditors) and team non-compete agreements.
10.why: Majorities can sit at board or shareholder level; board is faster. Non-competes are common in US-style docs but enforceability in Colombia is questionable — limit time and scope.

11.title: Right of first offer and tag-along
11.summary: Other shareholders' right to buy or join a proposed share sale.
11.why: Ensures that if founders sell partially, investors can exit on the same terms.

12.title: Board of directors
12.summary: Initial board composition with seats for investors and founders.
12.why: Ideal first-round size is small, ideally 3. The board decides whether to keep or remove the CEO — founders should retain majority control.

13.title: Drag-along
13.summary: Requires all shareholders to sell if a qualified percentage approves a 100% company sale.
13.why: Founders should be able to block an unwanted sale; this usually requires founder and preferred majorities, not investors alone.

14.title: Liquidity rights
14.summary: Forced exit mechanism if there is no liquidity between years 7 and 10 post-closing.
14.why: Funds need an exit horizon. Defines minimum return thresholds (IRR or multiple) before a demand sale.

15.title: Other matters
15.summary: Founder sale restrictions, term sheet confidentiality, and expiration date.
15.why: Confidentiality protects the negotiation; expiration forces closing or renegotiation within a reasonable window.
